_comment: The rule-code register: the AUTHORITATIVE list of every refusal code the content readers emit. It is an interface between two implementations, the game's C# reader and the pipeline's Python checker, and both test that the codes they emit are exactly these. Neither side renumbers a code; a new rule takes the next free number in its family, and codes are never reused. The table in CONTENT_MODEL.md section 5 is the human-readable index and cites this file as authoritative.

codes.summary: A required key is absent.
A value is not the declared type or shape.
A number has a fractional part. Every number in content is an integer.
A value that may not be negative is negative, as authored.
A key the contract does not declare, typically a typo.
An id does not match <namespace>:<name>, lower case.
The file's format string is missing, wrong, or a version the reader does not know.
The file is not parseable JSON.
A .json file in a namespace folder is not a content file name (e.g. models.json for model.json). Structural: nothing in a namespace folder is silently ignored.
A namespace folder holds no content file, so it defines nothing. Structural.
A reference names a namespace that no Content/<namespace>/ folder declares.
An id's namespace is not the folder its file sits in.
An id (or a template's unit type) is defined twice within its type.
A content file defines a player: id. That namespace is reserved for designs in a save.
A model and a variant share an id; designs are one id space.
A typed reference (class, model, trait, research) does not resolve.
The supersedes chain loops, including a model superseding itself.
A model supersedes a model of a different class.
A stat key is not on the stat surface of the entry's class.
A stat key is not in the engine vocabulary.
A cost names a resource pool not in the engine vocabulary.
A template names a unit type not in the engine vocabulary.
A facility row's kind is not an engine facility kind (vocabulary.json facility_kinds).
A settlement row's type is not one the map produces (vocabulary.json settlement_types).
A model or variant carries a trait its class does not list.
A trait legal on a class modifies a stat that class does not have.
A variant removes a trait its model does not carry.
A variant's model is a variant. One level only: traits compose.
A variant's delta makes a stat, cost or production value negative.
vocabulary.json differs from the engine's code. Only C# can see the enums.
Under the shipped power model, the authored 1930 base leaves a nation with supply below draw. A legal modelled state, so the game loads and reports it; our gate refuses it for OUR shipped files.
A pb: entry has no name, or a blank one. Mods may omit names; shipped content may not.
An engine unit type has no template row.
A template requires a class that no model belongs to.
No facility.json defines the tier and repair rules, or an engine facility kind has no row.
A facility lists a deposit its output does not produce.
A second facility.json, in any namespace, carries the tier and repair rules.
A settlement type the map produces, none included, has no row.
rates.json, combat.json or economy.json is defined in a second namespace.
rates.json, combat.json or economy.json is absent from every namespace.
